newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Malta puts EU application on hold, seeks new deal.
newsitem.headline: Malta puts EU application on hold, seeks new deal.

text.p: Malta said on Monday it had put on hold its application to join the 15-member European Union, preferring to work out a special deal for the small Mediterranean island.

"We don't see any importance in actually withdrawing our application. For the moment we're putting it in the deep freeze," Foreign Minister George Vella told reporters on the fringes of a meeting of EU foreign ministers.
"We're asking for special treatment, not privileged, but particular. We want a pragmatic approach, not fitting within existing frames, but one that can be of mutual benefit to both sides," he said.

Malta was among several countries asking to join the EU until elections four weeks ago gave the island's ruling Labour Party a mandate to change tack and seek a realistic partnership short of full membership.
"When the bottom-line was drawn we found out that it (full EU membership) was not in (our) best interests and that we should try and forge a new relationship," Vella said.

Vella said Malta's application would probably remain frozen for the foreseeable future, "in the region of five to 10 years", and this decision was unlikely to be altered "irrespective of what is fashionable".
"We will now be investigating all the avenues that one can explore. There is no ready-made framework that you can put on and say: 'this fits me'. We have to hammer it out."

Malta is seeking to build on existing ties with the EU on political, economic and security cooperation and wants to conclude an industrial free trade zone after a transition period of up to eight years, Vella said.
"We are specifically saying an industrial pact because if we had full customs union our prices would go up, affecting our costs of production and our competitivity."
A British diplomat said the European Commission would now pursue contact with the Maltese on the relationship. "Obviously that's the next phase," he said.
